author: Shiina LoSciuto
title: Family's life turned upside down after car crashes into home - NewsBreak
text:
By Shiina LoSciuto Leah Crowley ,
6 hours ago COVENTRY, R.I. (WPRI) — A Coventry family is still displaced nearly two months after a man trying to get away from police crashed into their home .
Diane Greenstein was on the couch when 50-year-old Derek DaCosta crashed a car into the front of her house.
“I was sleeping right here,” she told 12 News on Wednesday. “I’m lucky I’m OK.”
There are fractures in the walls, and the house’s foundation was shifted.
“The whole front of the house was pushed in,” Greenstein explained.
RELATED: Bodycam footage shows response to deadly Coventry crash On March 3, officers were called to Anthony Street after DaCosta allegedly forced two men and a woman into a car at knifepoint.
After officers pulled the vehicle over, the victims quickly jumped out. Body camera footage shows DaCosta speeding away as officers approached the car.
DaCosta then crashed the vehicle into a parked car and into Greenstein’s Main Street home. He was later pronounced dead at the hospital.
“We were just sleeping, now we’re living in an apartment,” Greenstein said.
The family has been left to deal with the lengthy and taxing process of going through homeowner’s insurance, car insurance and a police investigation.
“We’re paying a mortgage. My father, who stayed here, is now in a facility, which is expensive,” Greenstein shared. “We’re kind of in a holding pattern.”
The family is hoping they’ll be able to move forward with their lives soon, but work to repair their home has yet to begin.
“One person’s bad decisions changes everything,” Greenstein said.
